chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: I advise you with five things; if you ride your camels fast in search of them, they will be worthy of that.

No one of you should hope in anyone but his Lord, nor fear anyone but his own sin; no one should feel ashamed to say 'I do not know' when asked about something he does not know, nor should anyone feel ashamed to learn something he does not know.
And you are commanded to practice patience, for patience is to faith what the head is to the body; and there is no good in a body without a head, nor in faith without patience.
ai.seo_question: What are the five essential teachings for righteous living according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) outlines five essential virtues, emphasizing that hope should be directed solely to God and fear only to one's own sins, while encouraging intellectual humility by not hesitating to say 'I do not know' or to seek knowledge. He elevates patience (sabr) as the head of faith, a metaphor widely cited in Shia scholarship to illustrate that faith without patience is lifeless, much like a body without a head. This teaching underscores the practical integration of theological trust and epistemic honesty in the pursuit of righteousness.
